text: 3:06 I knew a Korean lady that offered to give me a bag she had stashed away in her closet. When I declined she took offense at this and decided right then and there that I didn't like her. It's definitely a cultural thing but it depends on who you're talking to. Receiving gifts from someone I just met feels uncomfortable. I prefer to slowly get to know people instead of being thrown into a relationship with gifts. People who throw expensive gifts at you often don't want to listen to you speak and it feels like they're trying to gain an upper hand in the relationship instead of having a fair relationship. I'd rather be able to express how I really feel at any given time instead of being silenced by indebtedness. It's not always the case but some people operate based on hierarchical power. If I haven't had much conversation with a person, it feels a bit off to be giving and receiving gifts. Unless it's a business relationship. It's understandable that in-laws do this because marriage is very often a business arrangement. Unfortunately those gifts probably often feel like you will never have a right to say how you really feel about the people who gave them to you. It's not a nice feeling.
